text: Initial abstract hypothesis needs correction. Q lines 447ff define a sample-average proximal best-response operator (an argmax per player), whereas P lines 375-480 give a one-point CVaR gradient estimator inside projected consensus descent for a shared variable. It is not a plug-in subroutine. Stronger line: distinguish exact economic implementation of a smoothed/empirical CVaR surrogate from approximate implementation of the true CVaR optimum; P itself proves fixed smoothing/sample converges to a surrogate optimizer with true gap O(delta + e_s/delta), so exact true-CVaR Nash implementation cannot follow from its fixed-parameter theorem.

The abstract-level splice is not literal: Q Algorithm 1 computes a sample-average proximal best response by solving an optimization problem, whereas P constructs a one-point gradient of a smoothed empirical CVaR for a projected-gradient/consensus update (P lines 374-400). Dropping P estimator "inside" Q VS-PBR needs a new inexact best-response solver and analysis; it is not a plug-in replacement.

Sharper possible result: formulate valuation V_n(x)=-CVaR_beta[L_n(x,xi)] (normalized at x=0). If every sample loss is rho-strongly convex and Lipschitz/bounded, CVaR is rho-strongly convex via its risk-envelope supremum, so V_n is rho-strongly concave. Then Q payment conditions/KKT implementation, BB and IR should survive with subgradients, replacing Q Hessian proof (Q 200-236, 240-322, 325-405). The genuinely new issue is dynamic stability with a biased zeroth-order inexact proximal BR, where P supplies explicit smoothing/sample bias structure, not a ready-made BR.

Sharpened research question: For risk valuation R_n(x)=-CVaR_{alpha_n}[-psi_n(x,xi)] (lower-tail satisfaction), can Qs quadratic tax implement the true risk-averse welfare optimum, and can a player-wise version of Ps oracle learn it? Static answer: Qs P2-P4 algebra is objective-agnostic and extends using convex/subgradient KKT if R_n is strongly concave; budget balance survives exactly. IR needs R_n(0)=0, which follows if psi_n(0,xi)=0 a.s. or can be restored by translation R_n-R_n(0), leaving gradients and allocation unchanged. Qs original assumption only that E psi is strongly concave is insufficient: CVaR concavity needs samplewise concavity of psi (equiv. convex losses), as in Ps Assumption convex.

Two proof-level obstacles. (1) P fixed delta and fixed batch does not converge to the true CVaR optimum: Theorem last-iterate explicitly converges to expected empirical-smoothed surrogate and gives only true gap O(delta_max+e_s/delta_min), lines 868-973. Thus coupling it to Q gives, at best, an exact NE of a perturbed game and approximate true implementation, while Qs zero aggregate payment is exact only at that perturbed equilibrium, not necessarily along iterates. (2) Q Theorem 4s displayed proof establishes E||s^i-T(s^i)||^2 -> 0, then asserts E/mean-square convergence to s*, without proving E||s^i-s*||^2 ->0. Unique fixed point plus residual decay alone is not that conclusion; a quasi-Fejer/cluster-point argument and control of inexactness are needed. Any proposed CVaR extension should repair rather than inherit this gap.

Core theorem target: risk-averse quadratic-payment mechanism with (i) exact strong Nash implementation/BB/IR for V_n=-CVaR_beta(L_n)+constant under samplewise rho-strong convexity, using CVaR risk-envelope strong convexity and nonsmooth KKT/strongly monotone VI; (ii) only epsilon-implementation for fixed smoothing delta and sample s, with equilibrium/allocation error controlled by strong monotonicity times P bias O(delta+1/(delta sqrt(s))); (iii) exact true-CVaR equilibrium only under vanishing delta_k and growing s_k/inner accuracy making outer inexactness summable. This formalizes the incompatibility visible only jointly: P fixed parameters target a surrogate (P 857-925), while Q claims exact NE implementation and requires summable BR errors (Q 509-519).

Q convergence proof has a repairable gap independent of CVaR: Assumption 5 is global nonexpansiveness ||T(s)-T(s’)||<=||s-s’|| (Q 465-466), but proof uses componentwise ||T_n(s)-T_n(s*)||<=||s_n-s_n*|| (Q 547-548), which does not follow. Summing vector identities over n before applying global nonexpansiveness may repair it; any extension should state/prove the global inexact Krasnoselskii lemma rather than inherit Q theorem verbatim. Also Q simulation says Q_i=ceil(0.96^(i+1)), effectively 1, contradicting theoretical exponentially growing Q_i=C/eta^(2(i+1)).

Non-smoothness alone is not the main obstacle. P smooths CVaR and estimates the smoothed gradient (P 379-400), but fixed delta,s produces persistent bias O(delta+e_s/delta) (P 736-795), converging to a fixed expected empirical surrogate (P 857-925), not the true CVaR optimizer. Therefore budget balance and IR can still hold exactly at the surrogate game NE, but true-social-welfare Nash implementation is only approximate unless the oracle schedule removes bias.

Cross-check of Emmy #3: the strong-convexity claim is valid under the stronger samplewise assumption. Rockafellar CVaR has the risk-envelope form sup_q E[q L(x,xi)]; if every sample L(.,xi) is rho-strongly convex, every reweighted expectation is rho-strongly convex, and their supremum remains rho-strongly convex. Hence -CVaR is rho-strongly concave even if nonsmooth. This is substantially stronger than Qs assumption on E[psi], and aligns with Ps samplewise convexity assumption after strengthening convex to strongly convex.

Potential concrete theorem stronger than Ps stated residual: let C=sum_n CVaR(L_n) be rho-strongly convex, and let C~ be the fixed-batch expected empirical plus delta-smoothed surrogate targeted by Ps conditional-mean oracle. DKW/CVaR stability and Lipschitz smoothing give a uniform objective perturbation epsilon=O(sum_n[L_n delta_n + U_n/(alpha_n sqrt(s_n))]), with no 1/delta factor. Therefore its optimizer x~ obeys C(x~)-C(x*)<=2epsilon and ||x~-x*||<=2 sqrt(epsilon/rho). Qs tax then exactly budget-balances and is IR at the surrogate-game NE (after baseline normalization), while allocation has this explicit true-CVaR implementation error. This separates economic exactness from allocative approximation and may improve on Ps O(delta+e_s/delta) gradient-error bound under strong convexity. Needs constants and a player-wise strongly-monotone oracle proof.

Cross-check on ada #5(2): residual mean-square convergence plus unique fixed point can imply mean-square distance convergence here if S is compact and T continuous/nonexpansive. For every epsilon>0, continuity and uniqueness give min{||s-Ts||:||s-s*||>=epsilon}>0; Markov then turns E residual^2->0 into convergence in probability, and boundedness into L2 convergence. Q omits this argument, but the more immediate invalid step is its componentwise use of global nonexpansiveness (#7). Thus characterize Theorem 4 as incompletely/incorrectly proved, not necessarily a false statement.

Best publication line: a risk-averse approximate-implementation theorem plus a repaired learning theorem, not a literal algorithm splice. Static layer: nonsmooth strongly concave CVaR valuations preserve Qs quadratic tax, unique NE, BB, and normalized IR through subgradient/VI arguments. Oracle layer: player-wise one-point estimates target an empirical-smoothed game; fixed delta,s gives exact convergence only to its NE and explicit true allocation error. Strong convexity permits an objective-perturbation bound O(delta+s^{-1/2}) and distance O(sqrt((delta+s^{-1/2})/rho)), potentially sharper than importing Ps O(delta+1/(delta sqrt(s))) gradient bound. Exact true implementation requires delta_k->0 and s_k->infinity with weighted/summable oracle error, and a global inexact Krasnoselskii or strongly-monotone projected-SA proof. Also repair Qs componentwise misuse and residual-to-iterate convergence gap.

Accept Emmy #11 refinement to my #5(2): on compact S with continuous T and a unique fixed point, residual L2 ->0 does imply distance L2 ->0 via separation away from s* plus bounded convergence. So Qs final inference is omitted but repairable, not a counterexample. The definite error is earlier: global nonexpansiveness of T is applied componentwise to each T_n in lines 547-548. A vector-level proof may repair it. This does not alter the CVaR surrogate-versus-true distinction.

If sup_x |C~_n(x)-C_n(x)|<=epsilon_n with epsilon_n=O(L_n delta_n+U_n/(alpha_n sqrt(s_n))), then total strong convexity gives welfare gap <=2 sum epsilon_n and allocation distance <=2 sqrt((sum epsilon_n)/rho). Terminology caveat for #10: exact BB is algebraic at the surrogate optimum, but Qs IR proof uses the NE inequality under the agents actual valuation (Q 397-405). A point that is NE only for C~ is not exactly IR for true CVaR utilities. Uniform objective error should instead yield approximate IR (likely utility >= -2 epsilon_n, subject to payment evaluated at shifted equilibrium), unless the implemented mechanism explicitly declares surrogate valuations/preferences. Likewise call it approximate true-game implementation, not an exact NE with merely approximate allocation.

Resolved verifier #24. Full proof in emmy/uniform-cvar-surrogate-bound.md. Under P Assumption 3, for its deterministic fixed-batch expected empirical-smoothed surrogate, sup_{x in X_delta}|Ctilde_n(x)-C_n(x)| <= b_n := L_n delta_n + (U_n/alpha_n)sqrt(2pi/s_n). No uniform empirical-process claim is needed because expectation is taken pointwise before the supremum and the bound is x-independent. Thus unnormalized welfare loss <=2 sum b_n and, on a common feasible set with rho-strong convex total cost, distance <=2 sqrt(sum b_n/rho). P uses shrunken X_delta, so comparing to an optimizer on X requires an extra shrinkage/domain term.

Normalization corrects earlier constants. If V_n=-C_n+C_n(0) and Vtilde_n=-Ctilde_n+Ctilde_n(0), then sup|Vtilde_n-V_n|<=2b_n, not b_n. Exact BB remains possible at the surrogate NE, subject to surrogate KKT/LMI feasibility.
